messages:
sre-bot: PAGE — container crashloop detected on shard r3-prod-12. Runtime process exiting with SIGSEGV in runtime_engine.so v2.1.7. Affected pods: 18/60 in gpu-pool-prod. Error rate ~22% for hosted text-gen requests. Pager escalated to oncall.

elaine: I'm taking this. Acknowledged oncall. Starting live triage.

elaine: Quick snapshot: crashes happen ~25-40s after container start, full coredump available on host when enabled. Repro local-ish on node r3-prod-12 with same model variant.

mohit: Noted. Can we cordon that node and drain? Prefer to evacuate gracefully then scale up warm spare nodes.
dina: I'll enable core_pattern and collect a gcore while we still have a crash reproducer. grabbing PID when it spins up.

elaine: Running quick checks — attaching logs.

kubectl -n inference logs pod/runtime-xyz -c runtime | tail -n 200
# last lines show:
# fatal: runtime_engine.so(+0x12a3f) [0x7f8c1a12a3f]
# SIGSEGV at 0x7fefc000

elaine: Also running: `kubectl describe pod runtime-xyz` — OOM not present, memory stable until crash. Points to null-deref in fused kernel path.

ops-bot: Runbook: https://internal.runbooks/release/runtime-crashloop (links to triage checklist).

mohit: Plan: 1) cordon r3-prod-12; 2) drain pods (graceful) 3) roll traffic to fallback variant (cpu-quant or v2.1.6 engine) 4) collect cores and kernel logs; 5) if crash persists across nodes, hotpatch rollback.

dina: Starting step 1/2: `kubectl cordon r3-prod-12` then `kubectl drain r3-prod-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` (doing a controlled evacuation).

elaine: Doing live traffic reroute: updating routing policy for pool-gpu-prod -> fallback pool-gpu-warm for 30 minutes.

support-lead: Customer impact — Support dashboard shows spike in 500s for ~400 customers, mostly during 16:23–16:36 UTC. Flagging top 10 affected tenants to CS.

mohit: Rolling a canary rollback to runtime v2.1.6 on small slice (5%) to validate stability.

elaine: Observability — token latency small increase but error rate dropping after reroute. Metrics: error-rate down from 22% -> 3% after eviction + rollback canary.

dina: Collected core at /var/crash/core.runtime. uploading to internal S3: s3://redwood-debug/r3-prod-12/5451236789-core.tar.gz (uploader started).

ops-bot: Upload complete. Correlation artifacts: core, dmesg, container logs, nvml logs. Link: https://s3.internal/redwood-debug/r3-prod-12/5451236789-core.tar.gz

mohit: After canary looks good for 6m, promoting rollback across pool. Scheduling rolling restart with 1 pod at a time.

elaine: Rolling restart in progress. Using `kubectl rollout restart ds/runtime-gpu --namespace inference` with maxUnavailable=1.

pm-raj: PM note — any customer-visible mitigations applied? Please post short blurb for status page for transparency.

support-lead: Draft for status: "Degraded performance for hosted text-generation between 16:23–16:36 UTC due to a runtime crashloop affecting a subset of GPU workers. Traffic routed to fallback variants and rolling rollback applied; issue mitigated at 16:36 UTC. Engineering collecting cores and investigating root cause. Customers with persistent impact will be contacted by Support." Please review.

elaine: +1. Published status update.

mohit: Final checks — cluster stabilized, affected pod count back to 0 crashloops. Some pods still draining off r3-prod-12, but we've evacuated all inference workloads.

elaine: Postmortem action items created: 1) reproduce with minimal model to pinpoint null-deref (assign dina), 2) add extra sentinel checks and ASAN-like tracing in fused-kernel path (assign runtime team), 3) add early-detection alert for warmup-period segfaults, 4) test rollback playbook and warm spares.

dina: I'll start a debug job to run under sanitizer builds against the fused-kv path and share logs.

mohit: Handoff — I'm primary oncall for the next window, leaving detailed notes in PagerDuty. If the cores show a memory corruption pattern, escalate to runtime eng and hardware lead.

elaine: Customer impact summary for PMs/Support: ~15% of customers saw elevated 500s for ~12 minutes; mitigated by draining node + rollback; no data loss reported.

support-lead: Notifying top affected accounts, asking engineering for ETA on root cause and expected fix timeline.

pm-raj: Thanks — we'll coordinate a postmortem and communicate any SLA credits if needed.

elaine: Closing live thread for now — will continue offline investigation. Tagging runtime-eng channel and assigning follow-ups. :thumbsup:

mohit: Thanks all. Handoff complete — leaving the incident notes and artifacts in the ticket.
